The result states what a stub in our loader must do on return (MMU and cache state, stack, which registers carry what) and which boot-args and ADT facts the payload cmdline actually contains (loader_return_after and the like), and names the transports that this contract makes possible and the ones it does not (video via the loader, S-Boot upload mode, USB gadget, storage write), each with what is unknown and the check that would resolve it.
Nothing is flashed, run or written on the phone. All claims are labelled source-review or host-test.

tasks.title: Simulate the payload kernel's bootstrap on the host: run start_first_cpu from the real payload bytes under a decoder-driven interpreter with an MMU walker, to checkpoints 1-5 and the return into arm_init
acceptance: An interpreter that executes the real payload bytes (decoded with capstone, executed by independent code) runs the kernel's start_first_cpu from the entry with the loader's real boot_args layout and the measured window (physBase 0x9de400000, kernel virt base 0xfffffff004000000) and reaches, in order, the five assembly checkpoints when the XNULDRST slot holds stub PA, checkpoint N and PA-VA; each stop presents x0=0, x1=0, x2=2, x3=N and a cleared SCTLR_EL1.M.

With the slot left at zero the same run falls through all five sites, builds the bootstrap tables, enables the MMU (SCTLR_EL1 write) and returns through its own `ret` to the virtual address of arm_init; every instruction fetch and data access after the MMU write is translated by a table walker that reads the tables the kernel itself wrote (TTBR0 V=P and TTBR1 KVA), and the translation of the kernel's own PCs and of arm_init matches window base + (VA - virt base). A deliberately wrong boot_args (wrong physBase or virtBase) is detected by the same checks, so they can fail.

The run states what the interpreter does not model (caches, the full ISA, timing, system-register side effects beyond the listed ones) and labels every result host-test/simulation, not hardware evidence. Nothing is run on the phone.
steps: Decode the start code range and list the instruction forms it uses
Write the interpreter and the table walker, run the real bytes
Add negative controls and document the model limits

tasks.title: Prepare the NAT-022 loader-diag-xnu-ckpt image: fill the kernel's XNULDRST slot, jump to the real entry, a return stub that reports checkpoints and exceptions, host-tested and held for an image-specific owner decision
acceptance: A deterministic hash-anchored loader variant fills slot [1]=stub PA, [2]=checkpoint, [3]=PA-VA (found by scanning the copied kernel segments for the magic, refusing unless exactly one 8-byte-aligned match followed by three zero words), keeps the kernel's own entry word (no entry stub), cleans the window after the fill and jumps to the real entry; every earlier image stays byte-identical.

The return stub handles reason 2 (assembly and C checkpoint) and reason 1 (early exception) and a held final stop: clears SCTLR_EL1 M/C, ic iallu, sets its own stack, draws new marker frames carrying reason, code, ESR/ELR/FAR where present and the log length, and never touches memory other than its own stack and the framebuffer/DECON registers already granted. Host checks: decoder-based interpretation of the stub, independent frame decode, alignment scan, reproducible build, package, gated session driver.

An image-specific decision request (SHA-256s, device access, what runs and what does not, risks, recovery, Not granted) is put to the owner. Nothing is flashed, run on the phone or jumped to before that decision.
steps: Add the slot fill, stub and marker kinds behind new macros
Host-check, build twice, package, gate the driver
Document and put the decision question to the owner
tasks.progress_note: Design fixed after reading patch_loader.py, xnu_stub.S, markerlib.c and the NAT-030 model: no entry stub (the kernel's own first word runs); slot filled by scanning the copied segments; return stub in the loader image saves x0..x30+SP+SCTLR+VBAR, switches to the loader stack and VBAR, draws a new CKPT marker, resumes asm checkpoints 1..4 (MMU off) through slot[2]=N+1, and holds at 5 (first MMU-on point; resuming there would need code in the kernel's TTBR0 map). C checkpoints are not used (not modelled past 10).

acceptance: From the real payload bytes (capstone cross-checked), list the kernel code reached from the continuation of asm checkpoint 5 up to C checkpoint 11 and inside loader_jump/loader_checkpoint: functions called, every system-register write, SIMD use, and every memory access that can hit a device (MMIO) or leave the loader's window, each marked modelled / not modelled by the NAT-030 interpreter; calls into gic_v3_irq_quiesce and its register reach are resolved or explicitly marked unknown.

Run 008 (decision 0016) results that constrain the design (checkpoint 5 reached with the kernel's TTBR0 identity map and TTBR1 as modelled; the stub holds there) are used; the NAT-030 model is extended only as far as the next run needs.

A design for resuming at checkpoint 5 is written and host-checked as far as the model allows: where a trampoline can live inside the kernel copy's identity-mapped range (the 725-NOP sled at the entry is the candidate), the SCTLR/M re-enable sequence, and the cache maintenance on the slot line with the order that cannot let a stale kernel-cached line or a clean overwrite the new value, plus the stop/hold policy for the first C checkpoint; every unmodelled step is listed as an unknown for the decision request.
No image is built for the phone, flashed or run here. If an image is proposed, a separate task and an image-specific owner decision (hashes, device access, risks, recovery, Not granted) come first.

acceptance: The SIMD instruction forms that the kernel executes between C checkpoint 10 and C checkpoint 11 (cpu_data_init, PE_init_platform(0, boot_args) and what they call) are implemented in a subclass of the NAT-030 interpreter (nat-030 files unchanged) and every implemented form is checked against Unicorn on randomized register and memory inputs; forms outside that list still fail loudly.

With them, the model runs the real kernel from the entry with a stop at asm checkpoint 5, the NAT-032 resume (slot[2] = 11, MMU-off branch to site5 - 28) and a C stop at checkpoint 11: either the C stop at 11 arrives (state at the arrival: registers, SCTLR/TCR/TTBR0/TTBR1/VBAR, the private block, loader_log length) or the first unmodelled or faulting instruction is named. The resumed run is compared with the uninterrupted run (slot[2] = 11 from the start) in registers, system registers and RAM at the arrival.

The path is reported as executed (function list in order, system registers written, memory outside the window touched, loader_log contents/length), not only as statically reachable; any MMIO-range access or panic call on it is a finding.
No image is built for the phone, flashed or run here; if the host run supports an image, it is proposed as a separate task with an image-specific owner decision.

A host model of the DWC3 device side (register file, event buffer, TRB processing for control transfers) and a USB host stub drive the engine in host tests: descriptor reads, partial reads, ring wrap/overrun markers, an exception frame, requests arriving while the engine is in its hold loop, malformed SETUP packets; mutation checks show the tests fail on seeded defects.

No phone is touched.

tasks.title: Stage-0 PID 1 for the next native run: on the critical path to Apple dyld/launchd, read the delivered root from inside the kernel instead of hashing a prefix. A static arm64 Mach-O (md0, as the NAT-077 probe) that (1) mounts /dev/md1 read-only with the donor's stage0 call (mount("apfs", "/redwood", MNT_RDONLY, "/dev/md1"), pinned donor SHA 87bf485), (2) lists a fixed set of paths of the iOS root (/sbin/launchd, /usr/lib/dyld, the dyld shared cache, a handful of frameworks) with st_size, (3) reads named files and prints their SHA-256 with ARMv8 SHA-256 instructions (read and hash timed separately, the dyld shared cache is in the unread tail), all under 55 s so loader_return_after (max 63 s) needs no keepalive, (4) prints exit status 81; plus the host-side expected values read by apfs_lib from the same image. Host-test only (Unicorn and the existing apfs_lib), no phone action
acceptance: Sources are the donor's stage0.c mount call and the NAT-077 probe's read/print scaffolding, pinned, each deviation listed; the SHA-256 code uses the ARMv8 crypto instructions and is checked against FIPS vectors and against hashlib on random buffers in Unicorn (the instructions are supported or modelled by an independent reference, stated); a plain-C fallback is kept for comparison only.

The host produces, with apfs_lib from the same padded image, the list of paths with sizes and SHA-256 that the probe must print (expected.json), and a comparator that turns the probe's console text into pass/fail per path; refusal classes are separate for: mount failed (errno), path missing, size differs, digest differs, timeout.

The probe is built with the project toolchain as a static ad-hoc-signed Mach-O and checked by the independent reader (no dynamic dependency); the time budget (read rate 33 MB/s measured on the S24 in NAT-078, hash rate by instruction) shows the chosen file set fits 55 s; the statement of what the host test does not show (the kernel's apfs VFS is untested on the phone) is in the README.
